transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, I guess I'm here because I just feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next. I can't really just... idle. And there's a new setup at work, which has made it a lot harder to hide lately. So... yeah. That's about it.

Can you tell me if you've felt this way—always needing to be doing something, unable to slow down—for as long as you can remember, even back in childhood, or is this something that started more recently in your life?

Yeah... it's been a while. Long before the job changed, anyway. 

I guess even back in grade school... I remember teachers writing on my report cards that I was bright, but careless. They said I talked out of turn a lot... had to be reminded to just stay with my work. So... yeah. It's not new.
Besides feeling restless, do you often find yourself fidgeting, having trouble sitting still, interrupting others, or blurting things out before someone finishes speaking?

Um... yeah, I suppose. Even when I'm trying to look calm, my foot is usually bouncing under the desk. Or... I'll be clicking a pen during a meeting or something. I don't really notice I'm doing it. But... yeah. I guess I do that.
Do you often find yourself losing track of things, forgetting appointments or tasks, or having trouble staying focused on things like reading or paperwork, even when you're not moving around?

Um... sometimes, I guess. Like at work... I might mean to call a customer back, or... answer an internal message after lunch. But if I don't write it down in more than one place... it can just sort of slip my mind until the next day. So... yeah. That happens.
Do these same difficulties—like losing focus, restlessness, or forgetting things—also cause problems for you outside of work, like at home or in your relationships?

I suppose so, yeah. Um... even at home, trying to unwind. Quiet stuff that’s supposed to relax me, like... reading, or trying to sit through a movie with my wife... it doesn’t last long. I end up shifting around, or... making comments, or just getting up to find something else to do. It's... hard to just sit.
Do you often experience excessive worry or nervousness about various things that seems to drive this restlessness, or does the restlessness happen even when you're not feeling anxious?
Um... no. I don't really think I'm worrying about things. I'm not a very anxious person. It just... it happens anyway, I guess. Even when everything is fine.
Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, do you recall having these same kinds of struggles—like being unable to sit still, blurting things out, or losing track of things?

Yeah... I suppose so. Um, it's been around a long time. Way before my recent job changes. I remember... well, in grade school, my teachers used to write notes on my report cards saying I was... bright, but careless. They said I talked out of turn a lot... and they always had to remind me to just stay with my work. So... yeah. It goes back that far.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports lifelong (since grade school) pattern of hyperactivity (foot bouncing, pen clicking, inability to sit still during calm activities), impulsivity (talking out of turn), and inattention (forgetting tasks unless written down multiple times, careless mistakes noted by teachers). Symptoms are present across multiple settings (work, home, relationships) and cause functional impairment (marital/leisure activities disrupted, work difficulties). Onset clearly predates age 12, ruling out adult-onset conditions. Restlessness is not attributable to anxiety, as patient explicitly denies excessive worry, making GAD unlikely. The combined presence of both hyperactive-impulsive and inattentive symptoms with childhood onset and cross-situational impairment supports a diagnosis of ADHD, combined presentation (F90.0).
